items.headline: Brent crashes 11.4% to $104.23, WTI -7.55% to $96.26 as Iran-Qatar talks raise Hormuz reopening hopes
items.summary: Iranian and Qatari negotiators held a third consecutive day of talks in Doha and developed a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if Washington lifts its naval blockade and oil sanctions; President Pezeshkian said Khamenei granted negotiators authority to pursue a deal with the US. The move unwound much of October's war premium (Brent had risen 13.6% and WTI 15.2% for the month) in a single session.
items.actionable: The Hormuz-risk premium underpinning XLE and the commodities sleeve is unwinding fast on diplomacy, not resolution -- Trump is still floating fresh strikes and Netanyahu is pushing to resume them after Tuesday's midterms, so treat today's drop as reversible rather than a new regime.

items.headline: Trump keeps Iran strikes 'on the table' even as talks progress; Netanyahu presses for action after midterms
items.summary: Despite the Doha diplomatic progress, Trump said the US had 'knocked out their navy, knocked out their air force' but still needed to handle 'one or two sites,' which he said could be done 'in 10 minutes.' Netanyahu reportedly pressed Trump to resume strikes once Tuesday's US midterm elections are past.
items.actionable: A credible but fragile de-escalation means the silver/gold safe-haven bid and the oil complex can both snap back hard if talks stall post-midterms -- don't read Monday's calm as durable enough to add risk into the Hormuz trade either direction.

items.headline: Gold rallies to ~$3,955-3,966 (+1.85%), silver to ~$50.7-50.8 (+3.6%) on dollar weakness as 10-yr yield hits 7-week low
items.summary: The dollar index slipped to roughly 101.7-101.8 and the 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.93%, a seven-week low, driving a broad precious-metals bid even as equities and oil traded risk-on around the Hormuz diplomacy. GDX rose 3.49% and SILJ 3.56% on the day.
items.actionable: The levered silver/miners sleeve is catching a rare 'everything rallies' day driven by falling yields and a weaker dollar rather than fear -- constructive for the GDX/SILJ/SLVP book, but running counter to the Fed's still-live December hike bias, so don't assume it's a clean new leg higher.

items.headline: Fed holds at 3.75-4.00%, Warsh gives no explicit December signal; hike odds near 76-85% into the Dec 8-9 meeting
items.summary: Chair Kevin Warsh and the FOMC held rates at their Oct 28 meeting without committing to a December move, but CME FedWatch and other futures-based trackers now price a roughly 76-85% chance of a quarter-point HIKE (not a cut) at the final meeting of the year under the Fed's new six-plus-two schedule.
items.actionable: The Fed is in a tightening-bias holding pattern, not an easing one -- Monday's gold/silver rally is running against the rate backdrop rather than with it, so keep duration exposure neutral and don't extrapolate the metals bid into a dovish-Fed thesis.

items.headline: US midterm elections today; prediction markets price ~70% odds of a Democratic sweep, futures rose into the vote
items.summary: Tuesday's midterms will decide control of Congress, with Polymarket/Kalshi pricing roughly a 70% chance of a Democratic sweep; a Morgan Stanley survey found 48% of investors flagged election-related anxiety given AI policy's outsized weight in an S&P 500 that is ~49% AI-linked. S&P 500 futures rose 0.49% and Nasdaq-100 futures 0.82% Monday heading into election day.
items.actionable: Midterms are historically low-impact for markets directly (S&P averages +15-17% in the following 12 months across the last nine cycles), but expect thin-liquidity air pockets in index futures Tuesday night/Wednesday morning as state results roll in.

items.headline: HK tech bounces hard: Tencent +2.2%, Xiaomi +6.1%, Hang Seng TECH +2.85% as Hang Seng closes +0.42% at 23,393.32
items.summary: Hong Kong's three main indices all rose Monday, led by a broad tech/brokerage/AI-hardware rally -- Tencent gained 2.2% and Xiaomi 6.1%, with Kuaishou, Meituan and Alibaba also higher, reversing Friday's AI-capex-driven risk-off carried in from the US.
items.actionable: HK tech is snapping back fast from Friday's AI-capex credibility shock -- a one-day bounce worth noting for the 0700/0981/1810 basket, but not yet confirmation the underlying capex-doubt overhang has cleared.

items.headline: SGX bank trio heads into results week (UOB Wed Nov 4, DBS Thu Nov 5, OCBC Fri Nov 6); UBS favors developers over REITs
items.summary: UOB reports first on Nov 4, followed by DBS on Nov 5 and OCBC on Nov 6, with UOB Kay Hian flagging wealth-management income likely eases q/q from Q2's seasonal peak even as it still rises ~11% y/y. UBS Global Research separately argued SGX-listed developers are better 'value-up' candidates than S-REITs, screening cheap at 0.7x price-to-book.
items.actionable: This week's three print days are the near-term catalyst for the SGX bank sleeve, while UBS's developers-over-REITs call is a direct read against the REIT-heavy side of the Singapore book.

items.headline: Correction: China's rare-earth truce runs to Jan 10, 2027, not Nov 10 -- but a new Jan 1 Pentagon-supplier ban creates a 9-day collision
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Bessent said on Sept 23 the US-China truce covering rare-earth export controls (originally set to lapse Nov 10, 2026) was extended to Jan 10, 2027, and MOFCOM confirmed the Kuala Lumpur arrangement extension on Sept 28. The real near-term flashpoint has shifted to Jan 1 2027, when NDAA Section 854 bars Pentagon suppliers from using Chinese-origin rare-earth magnets, creating a 9-day window before the truce itself expires.
items.actionable: There is no Nov 10 cliff for the MP/LYC.AX/UUUU watchlist as previously flagged -- the truce already runs to Jan 10, 2027 -- so the next real catalyst window is the Jan 1/Jan 10 turn-of-year collision, not next week.

items.headline: Binance's full zero-knowledge proof-of-reserves delayed from Monday to Tuesday Nov 3; BTC near $77-78k
items.summary: Binance's promised full ZK proof-of-reserves report following the $6.3B Lazarus/TraderTraitor hack slipped from Monday to Tuesday Nov 3, because generating the full proof takes roughly 40-50 hours of computation; the exchange says it has reserved over $6.34B to cover the shortfall.
items.actionable: Tuesday's delayed ZK proof is the key checkpoint on whether the Binance hack stays a contained, company-funded loss -- a clean proof removes a lingering sentiment overhang, a further delay or shortfall would reignite it.

items.headline: AI-capex credit stress persists: Meta's first negative FCF since IPO, mega-cap CDS at 2021 highs
items.summary: Weekend reporting confirmed Meta posted its first negative quarterly free cash flow since its IPO, and CDS spreads on Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle hit their highest levels since 2021, extending Friday's AI-capex-credibility shock from equities into credit markets.
items.actionable: The AI-capex doubt that hit tech equities and credit together last week is still unresolved underneath Monday's bounce -- a reason to stay cautious on capex-heavy mega-cap tech exposure, consistent with the book's cash-heavy, defensive tilt.

items.headline: Russia-Ukraine-US trilateral talks set for Abu Dhabi, possibly starting Nov 4, with no date yet confirmed
items.summary: Polish PM Tusk said ceasefire-adjacent talks could begin in Abu Dhabi on Nov 4, while Zelenskyy separately floated Nov 6-10 as the window negotiators might actually meet; the Kremlin says timing depends on battlefield conditions.
items.actionable: A credible Ukraine de-escalation track opening this week is a modest competing headwind for the gold/silver safe-haven trade alongside the Hormuz dynamic -- watch for talk-driven pullbacks in the levered silver book if Abu Dhabi produces concrete steps.
